Regularization is introduced whenever a theory gives ultraviolet (short-distance / high-energy) divergences that have to be tamed before one can interpret or renormalize the result.

(A) Quantum Chromodynamics – although asymptotically free, the perturbative integrals still diverge before one carries out a regularization and renormalization procedure.

(B) Classical Electrodynamics – the self-energy of a point charge diverges; one introduces a cutoff or smears the charge to make expressions finite.

(C) Quantum Electrodynamics – the textbook example of a theory that needs ultraviolet regularization and subsequent renormalization.

(D) Superstring Theory – the fundamental objects are extended (one-dimensional strings). This smearing over a finite length automatically softens the short-distance behavior, and perturbative string amplitudes are finite in critical dimension; no external UV regulator is required.

Hence, among the options given, only superstring theory is intrinsically UV finite and avoids the need for regularization.

Answer: D
